classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the highlighted axial triangle, use Pythagoras to find a diameter, halve it for the radius, and substitute into cylinder surface area while retaining precision.

content.prompt: Use Pythagoras’ Theorem $h^2=a^2+b^2$ to find unknown lengths and hence calculate the surface area of these solids. All units are in cm. Round your answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Tilted closed cylinder with its axis running down and right. The red dashed diagonal and lower-end diameter form the axial-section triangle.
spec.mathematics: Cylinder height 8 cm; axial-section diagonal 10 cm; unknown diameter satisfies d² + 8² = 10².
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given lengths 8 and 10 are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the diameter.
$$\begin{aligned}d^2&=10^2-8^2\\d&=6\text{ cm}\\r&=6\div2=3\text{ cm}\\SA&=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\SA&=2\pi(3)^2+2\pi(3)(8)\\SA&=66\pi\text{ cm}^2\\SA&\approx207.4\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Horizontal closed cylinder with narrow vertical elliptical ends. Red dashed diagonal joins the lower left endpoint to the upper right endpoint; a red dashed diameter completes the triangle on the right end.
spec.mathematics: Cylinder height 26 cm; axial-section diagonal 33 cm; unknown diameter satisfies d² + 26² = 33².
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given lengths 26 and 33 are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the diameter.
$$\begin{aligned}d^2&=33^2-26^2\\d&=\sqrt{413}\text{ cm}\\r&=\frac{\sqrt{413}}2\text{ cm}\\SA&=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\SA&=2\pi\left(\frac{\sqrt{413}}2\right)^2+2\pi\left(\frac{\sqrt{413}}2\right)(26)\\SA&=\left(\frac{413}2+26\sqrt{413}\right)\pi\text{ cm}^2\\SA&\approx2308.7\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Short upright closed cylinder. Red dashed diagonal joins the left top endpoint to the right bottom endpoint; a red dashed lower-end diameter completes the axial-section triangle.
spec.mathematics: Cylinder height 1.8 cm; axial-section diagonal 5.2 cm; unknown diameter satisfies d² + 1.8² = 5.2².
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given lengths 1.8 and 5.2 are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the diameter.
$$\begin{aligned}d^2&=5.2^2-1.8^2\\d&=\sqrt{23.8}\text{ cm}\\r&=\frac{\sqrt{23.8}}2\text{ cm}\\SA&=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\SA&=2\pi\left(\frac{\sqrt{23.8}}2\right)^2+2\pi\left(\frac{\sqrt{23.8}}2\right)(1.8)\\SA&=\left(11.9+1.8\sqrt{23.8}\right)\pi\text{ cm}^2\\SA&\approx65.0\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$
